item: a second stamp table article_www_stamps certifies places and entities under their own www engine id
key_paths: src/analytics/engine_identity.py src/analytics/store.py src/database/models.py migrations/versions/b3d8f1a6c4e2_article_www_stamps.py configs/www_indexer_pin.json scripts/indexer_pin.py tests/test_www_stamp.py
summary: R415 splits the engine identity in two. The keyword engine id (stamp article_index_stamps) no longer hashes the www-only modules (cities, entextract, locextract, whostore) or the city/place gazetteers; those form a separate www engine (WWW_INDEXER_VERSION, its own pin configs/www_indexer_pin.json, scripts/indexer_pin.py --engine www) with its own stamp table article_www_stamps (article_id, engine, inputs, stamped_at; create-table migration, no backfill) and its own inputs digest www_inputs_digest (the raw content column and country). index_article upserts the www stamp inside the same savepoint as the places and entities rows it certifies, so a failed savepoint leaves the previous stamp true of the previous rows; the new scope=www re-extracts places and entities only. Dates stay with the keyword stamp. Effect: a change to a place or entity extractor or a city gazetteer re-extracts only places and entities (the measured ~40% of a changed-rows run is the www stage), and a change to a keyword stoplist no longer re-extracts them. One-time effect: the keyword engine id changes, so old keyword stamps are refused once (R319), and every existing article has no www stamp until it is next indexed. Readers (the restore carry, the backlog counts) are a separate bundle (WAL); until they read the new table nothing relies on it. Stated limits: a --same recorded for a www change that altered output carries stale places; owes-nothing in a reader must mean both stamps.
